Policy Name: Cigna ACDF (CMM-601: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion)
Referred Sections: Compression at or behind vertebral body

Medical necessity indications.Guideline Category: Corpectomy for infection, trauma, tumor, or direct vertebral-body compression
Required findings: Severe neck pain or neurologic deficit (radiculopathy or myelopathy) attributable to infection, acute traumatic fracture/dislocation, neoplasm, or compressive lesion at/behind the vertebral body, with pain score ≥7/10 or functional limitation affecting ADLs
Objective neurologic deficits on exam (e.g., motor weakness, sensory loss, hyperreflexia, gait disturbance) consistent with the level of pathology

MRI or CT demonstrating pathology directly involving the vertebral body (e.g., epidural abscess, fracture, tumor mass, or bony compression) with concordant neural element compromise; for partial corpectomy, imaging must show that ≥50% of the vertebral body is involved

Failure of an adequate trial of non‑operative management (≥6 weeks of physical therapy, analgesics, and activity modification) unless contraindicated by acute infection, unstable fracture, or progressive neurologic decline
Patient must be nicotine‑free for ≥30 days verified by objective cotinine testing and have no uncontrolled behavioral health disorder that would impair postoperative recovery
All ACDF indications outlined in sections CMM-601.4, CMM-601.6, CMM-601.7, and CMM-601.8 (e.g., radiculopathy, myelopathy, adjacent segment disease, failed disc arthroplasty) must be satisfied
Documented radiographic evidence of segmental instability or neural compression requiring fusion
Conservative therapy documented for ≥6 weeks with persistent symptoms
Verification of tobacco cessation and behavioral health stability as above

Non-Indications: Corpectomy performed solely for osteophyte removal without resection of ≥50% of the vertebral body
Elective corpectomy for degenerative disease without infection, acute trauma, tumor, or direct vertebral‑body compression
Procedure attempted without meeting the prerequisite ACDF criteria (e.g., no documented neurologic deficit or instability)
Active tobacco use without documented cessation and objective cotinine test
Uncontrolled psychiatric or substance‑use disorder that precludes safe surgery
Insufficient trial of conservative management when not emergently indicated
Important criteria & exceptions: Partial corpectomy is acceptable only when at least one‑half of the vertebral body is removed; resection of osteophytes alone is excluded
Corpectomy must always be combined with cervical fusion to address iatrogenic instability
Objective cotinine testing (urine, serum, or saliva) must be performed within 30 days of the planned surgery
If the indication is acute infection, trauma, or tumor, the conservative‑therapy requirement may be waived
Multi‑level corpectomy requires separate justification for each level based on the above criteria
Documentation required: Operative report detailing extent of corpectomy (complete or ≥50% partial) and fusion technique
Pre‑operative cervical MRI and/or CT reports showing infection, fracture, tumor, or compressive lesion with measurements of vertebral‑body involvement
Plain cervical spine flexion/extension X‑rays demonstrating instability (if applicable)
Neurologic examination note documenting deficits and functional impact
Physical therapy and medication records confirming ≥6 weeks of conservative care (unless emergent indication)
Objective cotinine test result (urine, serum, or saliva) performed ≤30 days pre‑op
Behavioral health evaluation confirming stability or documented plan for management
Pathology report (if prior biopsy) confirming infection or neoplasm
